Definition: a primary particle; opposite, i.e. instead or because of (rarely in addition to):--for, in the room of. Often used in composition to denote contrast, requital, substitution, correspondence, etc.
BiblicalUsage: Anti is the small word that does heavy work: instead of, because of, in place of, as when Christ gave Himself a ransom for many and a man is told to render evil for evil to no man. The word marks exchange, one thing standing in the room of another.
TheologicalSignificance: A particle carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is in the exchange it names, that Christ stood in our place and gave His life a ransom for many.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
